title: ouCode fed to the matcher is majorCreditorCode; prosecutionAuthorityOuCode is never used for matching

oracle.activityBoundary: every callActivity argument and return value crosses oracle/lib/boundary.js
oracle.determinismCheck: the case was run twice at clockPinIso and the two document arrays compared

edits: hearing: prosecutionCases[0].prosecutionCaseIdentifier.majorCreditorCode set to "CDE04". Nothing else changed; prosecutionAuthorityOUCode stays "GAFTL00" as the fixture has it.

subscriptions: four copies of nowSubscriptions[0] of now-subscriptions-ir-sample.json, each with a fresh id / name / recipient.organisationName / recipient.emailAddress1, its informantCode removed, and then exactly one matching field set: informantCode CDE04, informantCode GAFTL00, selectedCourtHouses [CDE04], selectedCourtHouses [GAFTL00]. Every other field of the real captured subscription is unchanged, including applySubscriptionRules: false.

digests.convention: sha256 of the written file bytes — `sha256sum <file>` reproduces each value exactly

nodeEvidence.what: `subscriptionObj.ouCode = informantRegister.majorCreditorCode;` — the field named "ouCode" is populated from the major-creditor code.
`matchProsecutor(subscription, ouCode) => subscription.informantCode && subscription.informantCode === ouCode` — so informantCode is compared against a major-creditor code.
`informantRegisterFragment.prosecutionAuthorityOuCode = detail.prosecutionAuthorityOUCode;` — the OU code is carried on the fragment.

...and copied straight to the outbound document. A whole-repo grep for prosecutionAuthorityOuCode / prosecutionAuthorityOUCode outside test files returns only SetInformantRegister/index.js:14,46,62,87, OutboundInformantRegister/index.js:25, the model field, and an unrelated NOWs ProsecutorMapper — it is never read by the matcher.

assertion: Four subscriptions are supplied, all with isInformantRegisterSubscription true, all forDistribution + emailDelivery with a recipient. The hearing gives TFL majorCreditorCode "CDE04" and prosecutionAuthorityOuCode "GAFTL00". Assert EXACTLY: the TFL document's `recipients` array contains exactly two entries, in this order — the one whose subscription informantCode is "CDE04" (recipientName "match-informant-code-is-major-creditor") and the one whose subscription selectedCourtHouses is ["CDE04"] (recipientName "match-court-house-is-major-creditor"); and it contains NEITHER of the two subscriptions keyed on "GAFTL00", the real OU code. Also assert the TVL document, which has no majorCreditorCode, has NO `recipients` key at all. Write the assertion on recipientName so the failure message names which subscription leaked in. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK PIN IN THE PACK. The field name "ouCode" makes the Node code look like a typo, and a Java developer porting SubscriptionMatcher will be strongly tempted to match on prosecutionAuthorityOuCode "because that is obviously what was meant". If they do, this test fails — which is the point. D4 is a priority-2 defect: it is only allowed to change AFTER the SIT now_subscriptions verification named in the design doc §13 Q8, and then only via a doc/DEVIATIONS.md entry. Until that entry exists, matching on the OU code is a defect, not a fix.
